title: subnet-simmer-failure-and-host-pool-drain-harness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Build a safe, automated harness that simulates two related real-world failure modes not covered by existing chaos jobs: (1) progressive subnet-level isolation within a region (layered packet loss + connection churn) that causes slow fanout latencies and partial control-plane reachability, and (2) host-pool depletion via gradual eviction/return (simulated GPU driver OOMs and node cordon/drain cycles) to exercise circuit breakers and tenant-aware shedding.

Hypothesis: When a subset of racks/subnets degrades gradually instead of failing instantly, request tail latency and retry storms can silently burn SLOs before existing failover policies trigger. Combined with a gradual host-pool drain, admission controllers and circuit breakers may not trip fast enough or may over-react, causing wasteful cold fallbacks or cascading tenant unfairness.

Scope:
- Target: hosted inference control plane + serving edge within one primary region (can be repeated across secondary regions).
- Failure primitives: introduce per-subnet packet loss (0% -> 40% over 15m), increase TCP connection churn, inject 10-30% temporary CPU stalls on a subset of hosts, simulate GPU process OOM and graceful eviction workflow.
- Observability: collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, retry counts, circuit breaker state transitions, admission reject rate, cache hit ratio, and error-budget burn rate.

Safety & blast radius controls:
- Run only in a lab/staging cluster or in a dedicated canary tenant in prod (tenant flag required).
- Default run window: off-peak only; automated abort if error budget burn > 5% in last 1h.
- Max concurrency: 5% of active hosts in region.
- Auto-revert within 90s for critical path failure (control plane unreachable).

Test harness components:
- Injector service: stateful runner that orchestrates incremental network degradation and host drain signals via existing fleet-control APIs.
- Canary workloads: synthetic traffic generator that exercises short and long generation flows, long-context chat flows, and embedding/embedding-batch endpoints.
- Metrics collector: enrichment pipeline that tags metrics by tenant, route, model variant, and kernel type.
- Dashboard: dedicated chaos run dashboard (Grafana link placeholder) and a telemetry export to BigQuery for offline analysis.

Run phases:
1) Dry run (no packet loss, no evictions) — validate telemetry and rollback hooks.
2) Slow simmer (5% loss + 10% CPU stalls) for 30m — observe tail and retries.
3) Escalation (linear ramp to 40% loss + host evictions at 2% per 5m) for up to 60m — validate admission control and circuit breaker behavior.
4) Recovery & soak (revert degradations, observe recovery patterns) for 60m.

Acceptance criteria:
- No silent SLO burn: p99 latency increase must remain < 2x baseline or automated reroute must trigger within threshold defined by SLO dashboard.
- Circuit breakers: should open for problematic downstreams within configured window and traffic should be gracefully shifted to fallback variants without >10% extra token cost.
- Admission control: shed load in tenant-aware manner; top-5 tenants should not experience >3x latency increase vs baseline; global fairness metrics must be within target.
- Observability: every run should produce a reproducible telemetry bundle and a short human-readable run summary.

Deliverables:
- Injector code and runbook (repo PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/chaos-harness/pull/552)
- Grafana dashboard (draft link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/chaos/subnet-simmer)
- Runbook & safety checklist in Confluence (doc link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RIN/pages/12345678/Subnet+Simmer+Runbook)
- Postmortem template for unexpected SLO burn

Next steps:
- Design review with SRE and runtime teams (scheduled 2026-03-13).
- Build injector prototype and smoke test in staging by 2026-03-17.
- First controlled canary in prod (canary tenant) targeted 2026-03-19 if staging results are green.
